subject: Q3 deal-trigger: three-region dedicated SKU alignment and procurement cadence
messages:
From: Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@openframe.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@openframe.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity needs across regions for OPF-4729

Hi Karthik / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the OpenFrame product team is enthusiastic and we are moving toward a committed purchase decision for Q3. Procurement asked me to get firm on the region split & timing so they can start the vendor-side paperwork. High level ask below: can you confirm a recommended dedicated pool footprint for our expected steady-state and 2x burst across US / EU / APAC, plus any procurement/lead-time constraints we should know?

Estimated steady-state (avg concurrent inference):
- US: 350 concurrent threads
- EU: 120 concurrent threads
- APAC (SG + JP): 180 concurrent threads

Target start: 2027-08-15
Procurement window: they need pricing/sku and a rough lead-time by next Wednesday (2027-06-30).

Attached is our rough Q3 traffic forecast (OpenFrame_Q3_volume_estimates.xlsx). Would appreciate a short written recommendation that we can attach to the procurement packet.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if preferred.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Meyer
Head of Platform, OpenFrame

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@openframe.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs across regions for OPF-4729

Sarah — thanks for the forecast and the clear timeline. Putting together a concise recommendation for procurement, plus a conservative/optimized SKU split and the expected lead times.

Quick notes up front:
- We typically size for steady-state + 1.5x burst for guaranteed latency targets; if you need 2x burst in contract we can provision additional hot capacity but that increases monthly committed units.
- Lead times are primarily driven by preferred GPU type and regional availability. We can do an initial allocation using A100/80GB-equivalent on US/EU and a mix of A100/H100-equivalent in APAC for latency-sensitive workloads.

I attached a short proposal PDF (capacity_proposal_v1.pdf) that lays out a recommended pool per region and two commitment options (conservative vs. cost-optimized). Can you confirm: 1) whether burst must be guaranteed by contract or can be best-effort, and 2) final expected start date is 2027-08-15? Once I have that we can finalize the SKU counts and hand off to Marissa for allocation scheduling.

If helpful I can also produce a one-page procurement blurb that lists lead times and DocuSign-ready language.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs across regions for OPF-4729

Looping in a few sizing specifics from infra planning so procurement has actionable SKUs. My recommendations below intentionally aim for predictable unit economics while hitting your latency targets.

Option A — Conservative (guaranteed 2x burst):
- US: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (reserved), baseline autoscale to 12 for burst (2x).
- EU: 3 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes, autoscale to 6 for burst.
- APAC: 6 x H100-equivalent nodes (preferred for SG/JP high-concurrency), autoscale to 12 for burst.

Option B — Cost-optimized (1.5x burst, preferring spot-burst):
- US: 6 x A100-equivalent reserved, burst to 9 (spot-backed).
- EU: 2 x A100 reserved, burst to 4.
- APAC: 4 x H100 reserved, burst to 8 (hybrid spot).

Notes / lead-times:
- A100 availability in US/EU: ~2–4 weeks for reserved pools, H100 in APAC: 4–6 weeks for reserved (we can often backfill with smaller-capacity nodes for interim).
- Marketplace/vendor procurement (if using AWS marketplace private listing) can add ~1 week to DocuSign cycles.
- We recommend a 90-day procurement window from signed MSA to guaranteed reservation to give operations time to validate networking & VPC peering.

I also uploaded a short Mutual Action Plan draft (OPF-4729_MutualActionPlan.docx) to the shared Drive. If procurement needs a single-sentence technical justification for each SKU we can provide that as a one-pager.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@openframe.ai>, aws-marketplace@amazon.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Q3 deal-trigger: three-region dedicated SKU alignment and procurement cadence

Folks — final alignment before I send the procurement-ready pricing and DocuSign packet. Per Ben's sizing above, we will provision Option A if OpenFrame signs with a 12-month committed reservation to guarantee 2x burst. If they take Option B we need a 6–9 month commit and a burst SLAs clause (best-effort spot burst).

Action items before 2027-07-02 (procurement deadline):
- OpenFrame: confirm whether burst must be contractually guaranteed (Sarah).
- Karthik / Ben: finalize SKU counts and provide one-line technical justification for each region for procurement packet (e.g., "H100-equivalent for APAC to meet peak 95th percentile latency < 150ms").
- Marissa: hold tentative allocations for 10 A100-equivalent and 8 H100-equivalent nodes across regions and confirm potential reallocation windows.
- Priyom: flag this deal for priority tranche in the regional node backlog if commit is 12 months.

I've attached the DocuSign link for the draft SOW and a direct HubSpot reference for easy procurement tracking. Will follow up once Sarah confirms burst requirement.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/track/ABCDEF-OPF-4729
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/OPF-4729

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, GTM Strategy (Redwood Inference)
